items.headline: Overnight pulse (1:00 AM CT): DXY below 102.00 (~101.85, -0.33%) on AI-led risk-off; EUR/USD ~1.1194, GBP/USD ~1.339, USD/JPY ~157.4 post-BoJ, USD/CHF ~0.8214; Brent ~$116.14, WTI ~$103.43 on Iran-strike reports; gold ~$3,996-4,017; 10Y 4.98%, 2Y ~4.61% — levels are indicative index quotes, not executable prices
items.source: Economies.com / Lician / FXStreet / price-chart.com Asia Oct 30; ForexCommand NY-close roundup Oct 30; Treasury curve Oct 29

items.headline: Oil jumps in Asia — Brent ~$116.14, WTI ~$103.43 — on reports of possible renewed US action on Iran (WSJ: CENTCOM briefed Trump on options Thu); strike-timing claims (Oct 30-31) are single-source and unconfirmed; PBoC sets Oct 30 fixing at 6.7138, a large weak-side gap vs the 6.6548 estimate
items.source: price-chart.com Oct 30; BusinessLine Oct 30 — https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/markets/commodities/crude-oil-futures-rise-on-reports-of-potential-us-military-action-against-iran/article71643600.ece ; FXStreet Oct 30 — https://www.fxstreet.com/news/pboc-sets-usd-cny-reference-rate-at-67138-vs-67147-previous-202610300115

items.headline: Japan housing starts swing to a fall in September — down 2.7% y/y (vs +2.5% fcst, prev +6.1%)

BoJ HOLDS at 1.25% (8-1; Takata dissented for 1.50%) — Outlook Report judges underlying inflation 'generally consistent' with the 2% target, FY2027 core CPI median raised to 2.6% (from 2.4%); ETF sales accelerated to ~¥860B/yr from Jan 2027; December hike ~80%; Ueda presser 1:30am CT
items.source: Reuters Instant View Oct 30 + FXStreet post-BoJ — https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/view-analysts-react-boj-decision-keep-rates-steady-2026-10-30/

items.headline: Dollar slips below 102.00 on AI-led risk-off as yen holds ahead of the BoJ
Australia PPI a touch hot (+1.1% q/q vs 1.0% exp, +3.6% y/y), credit steady (+0.6% m/m vs 0.5% exp, +8.4% y/y) — no new signal before the RBA’s Nov 2-3 meeting
Japan factories beat, shoppers miss — IP +2.2% m/m (vs +1.3% exp, Oct outlook +5.1%) but retail +2.3% y/y (vs 3.3% exp, -0.7% m/m); jobs tighten to 2.4% (ratio 1.19) — mixed read hours before the BoJ
items.source: Breaking watch 19:32 CT Oct 29 (METI/Statistics Bureau releases)

items.headline: Tokyo core CPI in line at 2.6% y/y (headline 2.8%) as jobs tighten to 2.4% — yen barely moves into the BoJ

NY close (3:00 PM CT): EUR/USD 1.1162 (+0.08%), GBP/USD 1.3365 (+0.29%), USD/JPY 157.97 (+0.09%), USD/CHF 0.8262 (-0.23%), AUD/USD 0.7032, USD/CAD 1.3995, NZD/USD 0.5613; DXY ~102.15 (-0.22%) — dollar soft into the close despite the GDP beat; 10Y 4.98%, gold ~$4,030, Brent ~$113.82, WTI ~$101.09

Dollar range-bound into the NY afternoon (DXY 102.06-102.30) despite the GDP beat — EUR/USD dipped to ~1.1106 post-ECB then recovered toward 1.114-1.115; USD/JPY probed ~158.07 then hovered near 157.8 ahead of the BoJ; 10Y eased to ~4.98%

ECB HELD at 2.50% (deposit; refi 2.65%, marginal 2.90%) as expected — statement data-dependent, no pre-commitment; Lagarde presser: direction of travel 'clear', a hike was debated and unanimously deferred to December; Reuters sources: Dec 17 hike 'all but certain', pause thereafter as higher yields bite
Lagarde announces she steps down Feb 7, 2027, nine months early — succession process starts immediately; exit widely speculated, EUR little changed on the news

Post-7:30am CT data window (Finnhub/OANDA ~7:48am CT): EUR/USD 1.1138 (-0.14%), USD/JPY 158.06 (+0.14%), GBP/USD 1.3320 (-0.04%), gold ~$4,027 (-0.67%) — majors little changed; the 7:30 prints (GDP advance, Sep PCE, claims) were not yet verified from BEA/DOL at push time

US data block: Q3 GDP advance BEAT 3.4% SAAR (vs 3.2% consensus, prev 2.2%); Sep PCE in line (headline +0.5% m/m, +3.6% y/y; core +0.3% m/m, +3.1% y/y); claims 194K (vs ~199K, prev revised 195K); income +0.2%, spending +0.5% — December Fed hike pricing ~83% after the block

Thu morning data: EZ economic sentiment missed (96.9 vs 97.5, prev 97.9); UK money/credit softer (approvals 53.4K vs 54K, net lending £5.8B vs £6.2B, M4ex +4.0% y/y); Italian jobless 6.3% (vs 6.2% fcst) — soft reads into the ECB decision
items.source: European Commission / Bank of England / Istat

items.headline: Reuters Asia Oct 29: dollar steady after the Fed hold leaves the rate path murky — DXY 102.26, EUR/USD 1.1134 (-0.15%), USD/JPY 158.045 (+0.14%), NZD/USD 0.5621, AUD/USD 0.705; Warsh's silence on December read dovish (CBA's Kong); Dec hike ~78% (FedWatch); 2Y 4.712% (-2.3bp)

Reuters Oct 29 preview: ECB set to hold at 2.50% today (8:15am CT, Lagarde presser ~8:45am) — decision overshadowed by French bond turmoil and questions about Lagarde's future; poll 70/73 for hold, 64 see a December hike; money markets price ~3 more hikes to 3.25% by end-2027

Overnight pulse (12:40am CT): DXY ~102.18, EUR/USD ~1.1141, GBP/USD ~1.3327, USD/JPY ~157.75, AUD/USD ~0.7059, USD/CAD ~1.3981, NZD/USD ~0.5625 — dollar gives back its post-FOMC bounce into ECB day; US GDP + PCE land 7:30am CT
items.source: Samuel & Co morning brief Oct 29 + Finnhub/OANDA overnight — https://www.samuelandcotrading.com/morning-market-brief-29-october-2026-microsoft-beat-alphabet-miss-ai-trade/

items.headline: Gold slips as markets assess Fed signals, await US PCE — spot gold -0.7% to $4,037.98 by 0410 GMT; Dec futures $4,049.80; traders price ~78% Dec hike (CME) vs 84% pre-decision

Oil falls as peace hopes offset Middle East supply fears — Brent -1.1% to $114.10, WTI -1.3% to $101.45 at 0351 GMT; Vance letter sought to revive Iran talks (WSJ) even as the Saudi coalition destroyed a Houthi missile early Thursday

Warsh presser knocks dollar off its two-week high — DXY slides to ~102.05; 2Y pulls back to 4.726% (-1bp), 10Y 5.007% (+1bp); stocks +0.2% — Forex.com: Warsh fell short of a full hawkish December hint

FOMC HOLDS at 3.75–4.00% in a 10–2 vote — Cook + Hammack dissent for a +25bp hike; activity upgraded to 'strong' from 'solid', inflation 'remains elevated', no explicit December commitment; December hike ~86% (CME FedWatch via CoinDesk post-decision)

Loonie +0.1% to 1.4035 after the BoC hike; Can 2Y hits a 2-year high 3.441% (then 3.413%), 10Y +2.4bp to 3.885%; swaps price a further December BoC hike at ~45%, a second hike fully discounted by January (Reuters)
UK Budget lands muted: 10Y gilt -2bp to 5.323%, 30Y -3bp to 5.711%, sterling $1.3298, FTSE +0.1% — 'the boring budget bond markets wanted' (XTB); headroom £15B, OBR 2027 growth cut to 1.0%
Oil holds the rebound after EIA: Brent $115.66 (+$1.78), WTI $102.38 (+$2.48) at 11am ET; crude -1.9M bbl to 410.6M (4% below 5-yr avg), gasoline +3.9M, distillate -1.5M; WTI $102.82 into the FOMC

Morningstar/Dow Jones Oct 28: sterling fell to a 12-day low of $1.3269 in early European trade and 0.2% vs the euro to 0.8374 ahead of the Budget; 10Y gilt 5.354% (+1.2bp) — 'gilt markets are always a bit nervous heading into the autumn budget' (ING)

Reuters London morning Oct 28: sterling slips 0.1% to $1.329, a more than one-week low, and 0.1% vs the euro to 83.7p ahead of Healey's first Budget at 7:30am CT; 30Y gilt +2bp, having eased from its early-October high (highest since early 1998)
